summary: A HashMap matches keys to values, like names to scores. Use it when you look things up by a name instead of by a position.
notes: import java.util.HashMap is required. HashMap<String, Integer> uses Integer, not int.
put("Ben", 82) replaces the old value because keys are unique.
counts.put(food, counts.getOrDefault(food, 0) + 1) is the standard way to count items.
pitfall: int score = scores.get("Zoe"); throws NullPointerException because get() returns null for a missing key. Check containsKey() first or use getOrDefault().
